instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Who Cares More?
cards.instruction: Turn every favor, memory, sacrifice, and affectionate gesture into evidence that you care more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm putting our holiday things in order. I've kept twelve tickets. How many did you keep?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are in the album I made you. Don't pull it apart.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The album stays whole. I'll find it a box; apparently I'm keeping both our memories safe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought a box for it. It's under the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the album in, then. I'll write the dates on the lid. You won't even have to open it to remember our trips.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the book bag; you take the clothes. I care more about your back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me carry the books for a while.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And have you looking after me more than I'm looking after you? Keep the clothes; I'll slow down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put half the books in my bag, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. I'll pass you the paperbacks. The hardbacks stay with me.

cards.title: Still a Good Sign
cards.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me order us dinner. First time since the breakup, and you still groan at my waiter joke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I hoped you'd retired it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered the whole thing. We'll stick to food, then; I'll put the menu where we can both see it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just want to eat in silence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Silence it is. You still trust me to stay for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll move our dinner booking. You came to cancel in person; you still hate disappointing me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the third time. I feel awful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You wouldn't apologise three times if I didn't matter. We'll make it an easy supper next Friday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please stop holding Fridays for me. I can't promise anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right, no Friday booking. You're still looking out for my weekends.

cards.title: Affectionate Resentment
cards.instruction: Remain warm and familiar while letting old resentment sharpen beneath every caring gesture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit down, love; I've made your tea. No reminder needed, unlike my birthday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've brought cake. A month late, I know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your favourite, too. I'll cut you a proper slice; the birthday girl can have the corner. I've still got the candle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put it in your slice. I'll sing now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll hold the plate up for you, love. A month of waiting and I finally get to hear it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Get into bed, love; I've warmed your side. No forty-minute wait here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could have picked me up instead of leaving me at that taxi rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I could. I'll get another blanket. I remember how cold it was outside your office last Christmas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologised. Could you just warm my feet?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come here, love. Both feet. I wouldn't leave any part of you waiting that long.

cards.title: Relationship Ledger
cards.instruction: Price closeness, forgiveness, and support in favors, sacrifices, access, and future loyalty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to my opening and I'll call our argument settled. Mum can stop hearing about it over lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought forgiveness was a gift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It is. I'll hand it over beside my paintings. You needn't make a speech; just be there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm working that night. I could help hang them on Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sunday works. Hanging gets us speaking again. Help take them down after the exhibition and I'll give Mum something else to hear about.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One Sunday visit a month and you get the spare key back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I work Sundays. I just need to collect my records.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Saturday lunch, then. That gets you through the front door; the records are in the sitting room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring enough lunch for both of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That gets you the records. Stay for one side of an album and I'll help carry the boxes.

cards.title: Closer on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to repair the relationship while redefining closeness around the boundaries that benefit you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, let's reconnect. I'll come for dinner and leave at ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to discuss why you left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Put that before pudding so we finish on something nice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if I'm still upset at ten?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll book another dinner. I'll bring the food next time, but we'll still finish at ten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like a weekend to patch things up. I'll book separate rooms, and we'll keep the old arguments out of dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The old arguments are why we need the weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me the worst of it over coffee. I'll leave the afternoon free for a walk together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't get through everything over coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the rest by email. I can take it a bit at a time, and we can still have our walk.
